name: Pulp
hook: Jarvis Cocker started the band as a schoolboy in Sheffield and spent fifteen years turning it into Britpop's sharpest class commentary.
blurb: Jarvis Cocker started Pulp while still at school in Sheffield in 1978, but the band didn't become famous until the mid-1990s, when 'Common People' (1995) turned a sharp, specific story about rich people playing at being poor into one of the era's biggest hits. More than fifteen years between forming and success is unusual even in British music, and it shaped Cocker's songwriting into something more specific and more aware of class than most of his Britpop peers. Critics have often compared his witty, observational songwriting and his persona to the Kinks' Ray Davies, in one widely repeated line calling Pulp "the Kinks" to Blur and Oasis's Beatles and Stones.

signatureTracks.title: Common People
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A specific, class-conscious narrative built the way a Kinks song is built: one character, one situation, observed closely rather than generalized.

signatureTracks.title: Disco 2000
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The other half of Pulp's commercial peak, trading "Common People"'s anger for wistful, very English nostalgia.
